sources.claim: Buolamwini and Gebru (2018), "Gender Shades": three commercial gender-classification systems tested in 2017-2018 had error rates up to 34.7 percent for darker-skinned women versus at most 0.8 percent for lighter-skinned men. The finding is about those systems at that time.

Koenecke et al. (PNAS, 2020), "Racial disparities in automated speech recognition": five commercial speech-recognition systems had an average word error rate of 0.35 for Black speakers versus 0.19 for white speakers in the studied interviews. The finding is about those systems and speakers.

sections.skill: Compare error rates across groups and describe a disparity accurately

questions.prompt: What is an error rate?

choices.text: The share of cases a system gets wrong
The total number of people who used the system on a single day

questions.correct_answer: The share of cases a system gets wrong
questions.intro: An ERROR RATE is the share of cases a system gets wrong. A system can have a good average error rate but very different rates for different groups, called a DISPARITY. Studies have measured this. "Gender Shades" (Buolamwini and Gebru, 2018) found three commercial gender-classification systems had error rates up to 34.7 percent for darker-skinned women versus at most 0.8 percent for lighter-skinned men. A 2020 study of five speech-recognition systems found an average word error rate of 0.35 for Black speakers versus 0.19 for white speakers. Findings describe those systems at that time.

questions.prompt: What is Group X's error rate?

choices.text: 94%, since that is the share of words that the app read correctly for Group X

questions.intro: Error rate = errors / total cases. Compare groups two ways: the DIFFERENCE in percentage points (subtract) and the RATIO (divide). Example: a reader app misreads 6 of 100 words for Group X (6%) and 18 of 100 for Group Y (18%). Difference: 18 - 6 = 12 percentage points. Ratio: 18 / 6 = 3 times. Both are true; report the numbers so readers can judge.

questions.prompt: What is the difference in percentage points?

choices.text: 3, because Group Y has three times as many errors as Group X on the same words

questions.prompt: Which statement overstates a finding?

choices.text: "In this 2020 study, five systems had higher error rates for one group of speakers."
"All AI is biased against this group."
"The tested system erred more for Group B."

questions.correct_answer: "All AI is biased against this group."
questions.intro: Describe disparities accurately. Say WHICH systems, WHEN, and WHAT was measured. "Twice the error rate" and "16 percentage points higher" can describe the same gap in different ways; choose the clearer one and give the numbers. Avoid overstating ("all AI is biased against X") or dismissing ("it is fixed now") without new evidence. Systems change, so newer tests may show smaller or larger gaps.

questions.prompt: Which statement dismisses a finding without evidence?

choices.text: "A 2024 retest of the same systems found the gap had narrowed to 3 points."
"That was years ago; it's fixed now."

questions.correct_answer: "That was years ago; it's fixed now."
